claim: A donor with a single SV40 PA termination signal sequence without the modified exon (mutExon) in its Ne-cassette was not sufficient to efficiently stop target gene transcription.
source: In the initial experiments, we used a donor with a single SV40 PA termination signal sequence without the modified exon (mutExon) in its Ne-cassette. Using such donors, we were able to isolate stable integrations at the kctd10 locus and observed the correct expression pattern of tdGFP. However, after Cre mRNA injection, all the injected embryos resulting from the incrosses of such heterozygous F1 fish developed normally, although the green fluorescent signal was no longer detectable in most of the embryos, indicating the successful and efficient removal of the Po-cassette. These results suggest that the single SV40 PA signal might not be strong enough to efficiently stop target gene transcription; thus, either multiple copies of the transcription termination sequences are necessary, or the modified exon (mutExon) following the PA sequence might be indispensable for efficiently disrupting target gene expression in our strategy (data not shown).
evidence: This is an inference from experimental observations with a simplified donor design.

evidence: This is a quantitative experimental observation supported by imaging data in Figure 4—figure supplement 1E and citations to prior work.

claim: All the defective embryos for the sox10 geno-tagging experiment exclusively showed green fluorescent signals, indicating that they were most likely homozygous for the sox10NeG allele.
source: Furthermore, 24.6% (56/228) of the injected embryos exhibited extensive loss of pigmentation at 48 hpf, recapitulating the phenotype reported previously for the sox10 mutant colourless (Dutton et al., 2001a; Dutton et al., 2001b), and all these defective embryos exclusively showed green fluorescent signals, indicating that they were most likely homozygous for the sox10NeG allele (Figure 4—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is an observation and inference about genotypes based on fluorescence patterns, supported by data in Figure 4—figure supplement 1E.

claim: Genotyping results confirmed that all the abnormal embryos were sox10PoR-NeG/PoR-NeG homozygotes before Cre injection and that all the normal embryos contained at least one wild-type sox10 allele.
source: Genotyping results confirmed that all the abnormal embryos were sox10PoR-NeG/PoR-NeG homozygotes before Cre injection and that all the normal embryos contained at least one wild-type sox10 allele (Figure 4—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: This is a finding from genotyping analysis, supported by data in Figure 4—figure supplement 1F.

claim: There was no significant difference in mRNA levels between the sox10 wild-type allele and the geno-tagging allele without Cre mRNA injection.
source: As expected, there was no significant difference in mRNA levels between the sox10 wild-type allele and the geno-tagging allele without Cre mRNA injection, while the expression of the sox10 geno-tagging allele was significantly decreased after Cre-induced excision of the Po-cassette (Figure 4—figure supplement 1G).
evidence: This is a finding from qRT-PCR analysis, supported by data in Figure 4—figure supplement 1G.

claim: The expression of the sox10 geno-tagging allele was significantly decreased after Cre-induced excision of the Po-cassette.
source: As expected, there was no significant difference in mRNA levels between the sox10 wild-type allele and the geno-tagging allele without Cre mRNA injection, while the expression of the sox10 geno-tagging allele was significantly decreased after Cre-induced excision of the Po-cassette (Figure 4—figure supplement 1G).
evidence: This is a finding from qRT-PCR analysis, supported by data in Figure 4—figure supplement 1G.

claim: The transcription level of sox10 in the sox10NeG/NeG homozygous mutant embryos decreased by ~25 fold compared with wild-type embryos.
source: The transcription level of sox10 in the sox10NeG/NeG homozygous mutant embryos obtained by Cre-induced Po-cassette excision in the sox10PoR-NeG/PoR-NeG embryos decreased by ~25 fold compared with wild-type embryos, further proved the strong mutagenesis effect of the sox10NeG allele (Figure 4—figure supplement 1H).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from qRT-PCR analysis, supported by data in Figure 4—figure supplement 1H.

claim: The sox10NeG allele has a strong mutagenesis effect.
source: The transcription level of sox10 in the sox10NeG/NeG homozygous mutant embryos obtained by Cre-induced Po-cassette excision in the sox10PoR-NeG/PoR-NeG embryos decreased by ~25 fold compared with wild-type embryos, further proved the strong mutagenesis effect of the sox10NeG allele (Figure 4—figure supplement 1H).
evidence: This is an inference from qRT-PCR data showing greatly reduced transcript levels, supported by Figure 4—figure supplement 1H.

claim: The results with the sox10 locus demonstrated the universality and high efficiency of the geno-tagging strategy.
source: Taken together, these results demonstrated the universality and high efficiency of our geno-tagging strategy.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion drawn from the experimental results with the sox10 geno-tagging allele.

claim: Three levels of complex genome modifications could be achieved in zebrafish by using the dual-cassette donor method: (i) one-step generation of conditional knockout alleles through targeted insertion; (ii) simultaneous fluorescent labeling of CKO alleles to achieve a gene tagging effect; (iii) differential labeling of two different alleles (normal vs defective) to achieve a geno-tagging effect.
source: In summary, we reported a highly efficient knockin strategy based on the special design of multipurpose dual-cassette PoNe donors and NHEJ-mediated targeted insertion, facilitated by the CRISPR/Cas system. Three levels of complex genome modifications could be achieved in zebrafish by using this method: (i) one-step generation of conditional knockout alleles through targeted insertion; (ii) simultaneous fluorescent labeling of CKO alleles to achieve a gene tagging effect as well as labeling of the cells expressing the target gene, through the incorporation of an in-frame fluorescent reporter gene (tdTomato or tdGFP) in the positive-cassette of the donor (the feasibility of this dual-function 'two-in-one' KI allele strategy was demonstrated at zebrafish tbx5a and kctd10 loci); (iii) differential labeling of two different alleles (normal vs defective) to achieve a geno-tagging effect via the differential labeling of the two cassettes (Po- vs Ne-cassette) in the donor with two different fluorescent reporters.
evidence: This is a summary of the main findings and capabilities of the method developed in the study.

claim: The geno-tagging strategy enables the conditional switching of the fluorescent reporters and, thus, the discrimination of cells with three different genotypes (homozygous normal, heterozygote, and homozygous mutant/defective).
source: This advanced strategy enables the conditional switching of the fluorescent reporters and, thus, the discrimination of cells with three different genotypes (homozygous normal, heterozygote, and homozygous mutant/defective).
evidence: This is a statement about the capabilities of the geno-tagging strategy, supported by experimental data.

claim: The conditional coupled geno-tagging alleles were successfully generated at the tbx5a and sox10 loci in zebrafish and demonstrated the fluorescent reporter switch in response to Cre recombinase treatment.
source: We successfully generated such conditional coupled geno-tagging alleles at the tbx5a and sox10 loci in zebrafish and demonstrated the fluorescent reporter switch in response to Cre recombinase treatment.
evidence: This is a summary of the experimental achievements with the geno-tagging strategy.

claim: Previously reported KI techniques usually cannot distinguish cells or tissues with different genotypes, which limits the in-depth study of gene functions.
source: However, previously reported KI techniques usually cannot distinguish cells or tissues with different genotypes, which limits the in-depth study of gene functions.
evidence: This is a statement about limitations of prior KI techniques, based on knowledge of the field.

claim: The geno-tagging technique allows the real-time labeling and discrimination of knockout cells or tissues from normal ones to trace and compare their fates in vivo.
source: Fluorescence label switching, together with conditional gene knockout, not only allows the real-time labeling and discrimination of knockout cells or tissues from normal ones to trace and compare their fates in vivo but can even go further, potentially labeling different alleles with different fluorescent reporters.
evidence: This is a statement about the capabilities and potential applications of the geno-tagging technique.

claim: The geno-tagging strategy can potentially label different alleles with different fluorescent reporters, allowing researchers to easily determine and follow the genotype of each allele and each cell.
source: Fluorescence label switching, together with conditional gene knockout, not only allows the real-time labeling and discrimination of knockout cells or tissues from normal ones to trace and compare their fates in vivo but can even go further, potentially labeling different alleles with different fluorescent reporters. In this manner, one can easily determine and follow the genotype of each allele and each cell.
evidence: This is a statement about the potential capabilities of the geno-tagging technique.

claim: The original single-fluorescent-reporter version of the dual-cassette donor might trigger genetic compensation since it contains a mutExon bearing a premature stop codon in its Ne-cassette.
source: In addition, there is another potential advantage of the geno-tagging strategy due to the special design of the Ne-cassette in the donor. While the original single-fluorescent-reporter version of the dual-cassette donor might trigger genetic compensation since it contains a mutExon bearing a premature stop codon in its Ne-cassette, the mutant alleles produced through the geno-tagging KI strategy, which does not contain a premature stop codon to disrupt the target gene, are likely exempted from the disturbance caused by the genetic compensation response, thus simplifying as well as consolidating subsequent phenotype analyses.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about a potential disadvantage of the original donor design, based on knowledge about genetic compensation.

claim: The mutant alleles produced through the geno-tagging KI strategy are likely exempted from the disturbance caused by the genetic compensation response.
source: In addition, there is another potential advantage of the geno-tagging strategy due to the special design of the Ne-cassette in the donor. While the original single-fluorescent-reporter version of the dual-cassette donor might trigger genetic compensation since it contains a mutExon bearing a premature stop codon in its Ne-cassette, the mutant alleles produced through the geno-tagging KI strategy, which does not contain a premature stop codon to disrupt the target gene, are likely exempted from the disturbance caused by the genetic compensation response, thus simplifying as well as consolidating subsequent phenotype analyses.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about an advantage of the geno-tagging strategy, based on inference from the donor design.

claim: The authors recommend the use of the geno-tagging donor for the generation of CKO alleles coupled with gene or allele labeling effects.
source: Therefore, we recommend the use of the geno-tagging donor for the generation of CKO alleles coupled with gene or allele labeling effects.
evidence: This is a recommendation based on the advantages of the geno-tagging strategy.

claim: More polyA signals seem to be more effective for efficient termination of transcription.
source: Regarding polyA signals, in principle, more polyA signals seem to be more effective for efficient termination of transcription (Ni et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a statement about the relationship between polyA signal number and transcription termination efficiency, supported by a citation.

claim: There are potential disadvantages of employing two 8xPA sequences, each containing eight tandem repeats of the ~160 bp polyA signal sequence, concerning stability.
source: However, there are potential disadvantages of employing two 8xPA sequences, each containing eight tandem repeats of the ~160 bp polyA signal sequence, concerning stability.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about potential problems with using multiple polyA repeats.

claim: The repeats within each 8xPA sequence might be reduced during expansion and/or passaging to the next generations of the sox10PoR-NeG allele.
source: The repeats within each 8xPA sequence might be reduced during expansion and/or passaging to the next generations of the sox10PoR-NeG allele; on the other hand, the sequence flanked by the two 8xPA sequences (containing the downstream loxP and Ne-cassette) might be lost due to occasional recombination of the two 8xPA sequences, leading to the abolition of the CKO and fluorescence-switch effects.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about potential instability issues with the 8xPA design.

claim: The sequence flanked by the two 8xPA sequences might be lost due to occasional recombination of the two 8xPA sequences, leading to the abolition of the CKO and fluorescence-switch effects.
source: The repeats within each 8xPA sequence might be reduced during expansion and/or passaging to the next generations of the sox10PoR-NeG allele; on the other hand, the sequence flanked by the two 8xPA sequences (containing the downstream loxP and Ne-cassette) might be lost due to occasional recombination of the two 8xPA sequences, leading to the abolition of the CKO and fluorescence-switch effects.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about potential instability issues with the 8xPA design.

claim: The authors recommend beginning with the construction of the donor with 2PA, then testing its effect in founder embryos to determine whether this is sufficient to stop the expression of the second fluorescent reporter, and introducing more polyA signals when necessary.
source: Practically, since different target genes may have very different expression patterns and regulation properties, for each particular target gene, we recommend beginning with the construction of the donor with 2PA, then testing its effect in founder embryos to determine whether this is sufficient to stop the expression of the second fluorescent reporter, and introducing more polyA signals when necessary.
evidence: This is a practical recommendation based on the authors' experience with different donor designs.

claim: Germline transmission is crucial for the successful establishment of stable KI transgenic fish lines.
source: Germline transmission is crucial for the successful establishment of stable KI transgenic fish lines.
evidence: This is a statement about the importance of germline transmission, based on established knowledge.

claim: There is a strong correlation between the efficient germline transmission and correct insertion of KI donors in somatic tissues.
source: Interestingly, our results indicate a strong correlation between the efficient germline transmission and correct insertion of KI donors in somatic tissues.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental observations comparing different screening methods.

claim: High-efficiency germline recovery of the KI events was observed after preselection for mosaic founders that acquired the correct donor insertions in somatic tissues by selecting either embryos on the basis of fluorescent reporter signals or adult fish on the basis of fin clip junction PCR.
source: We observed high-efficiency germline recovery of the KI events after preselection for mosaic founders that acquired the correct donor insertions in somatic tissues by selecting either embryos on the basis of fluorescent reporter signals or adult fish on the basis of fin clip junction PCR.
evidence: This is a summary of findings about efficient germline recovery methods, supported by experimental data.

claim: More than 50% (5/9) of the fluorescent reporter-positive F0 fish successfully transmitted the KI alleles to their progeny for the tbx5a PoR-Ne KI fish line.
source: During the construction of the tbx5a PoR-Ne KI fish line, approximately 15% of F0 embryos showed the expected tdTomato expression after the injection of the donor together with the Cas9/gRNA system. More than 50% (5/9) of these fluorescent reporter-positive F0 fish successfully transmitted the KI alleles to their progeny.
evidence: This is a quantitative finding about germline transmission efficiency with embryo preselection.

claim: No germline transmission events were identified in the 40 founders negative for the somatic cell expression of tdTomato for the tbx5a PoR-Ne KI fish line.
source: In contrast, no germline transmission events were identified in the 40 founders negative for the somatic cell expression of tdTomato.
evidence: This is an experimental observation supporting the correlation between F0 fluorescence and germline transmission.

claim: Approximately half (10/21) of the embryonic stage preselected founders showed germline transmission of the sox10 geno-tagging KI alleles.
source: Similarly, approximately half (10/21) of the embryonic stage preselected founders showed germline transmission of the sox10 geno-tagging KI alleles.
evidence: This is a quantitative finding about germline transmission efficiency with embryo preselection for the sox10 locus.

claim: For the screening of tbx5a PoR-NeG geno-tagging KI fish, 6 out of 48 founders were positive for donor insertions in fin clip somatic tissue by junction PCR.
source: For the screening of tbx5a PoR-NeG geno-tagging KI fish, we preselected adult fish for somatic cell integration by junction PCR of fin clips and found that 6 out of 48 founders were positive for donor insertions in this somatic tissue.
evidence: This is a quantitative finding about the efficiency of fin clip junction PCR screening.

claim: Among the 6 fin clip junction PCR-positive founders for tbx5a PoR-NeG, 2 out of 5 positive founders were also positive for germline transmission.
source: Among these founders, 2 out of 5 positive founders were also positive for germline transmission.
evidence: This is a quantitative finding about germline transmission efficiency with fin clip preselection.

claim: None of the 20 founders negative by fin clip junction PCR transmitted a KI donor to their offspring for the tbx5a PoR-NeG screening.
source: Not surprisingly, we also screened for germline transmission in 20 founders negative by fin clip junction PCR and found that none of them transmitted a KI donor to their offspring.
evidence: This is an experimental observation supporting the correlation between fin clip PCR results and germline transmission.

claim: To achieve efficient recovery of germline-transmissible KI alleles, the authors strongly recommend the preselection of F0 embryos according to fluorescent signals or adults on the basis of fin clip junction PCR and then screening only these founders in germline transmission analysis.
source: In summary, to achieve efficient recovery of germline-transmissible KI alleles, we strongly recommend the preselection of F0 embryos according to fluorescent signals or adults on the basis of fin clip junction PCR and then screening only these founders in germline transmission analysis.
evidence: This is a recommendation based on the experimental findings about efficient germline recovery methods.

claim: Compared with traditional KI strategies, which generally adopt donors containing a single functional cassette, the dual-cassette donor design provides more flexibility to achieve complex genome manipulation, enabling a variety of applications.
source: Compared with traditional KI strategies, which generally adopt donors containing a single functional cassette, our dual-cassette donor design provides more flexibility to achieve complex genome manipulation, enabling a variety of applications.
evidence: This is a comparative statement about the advantages of the dual-cassette donor design.

claim: The dual-cassette donor system could theoretically be expanded to other applications after further modification, such as to simulate precise genome modifications, achieve conditional gene rescue or differentiate and analyze maternal, zygotic and paternal gene expression and activity.
source: In addition to coupling conditional knockout with gene-labeling or geno-tagging, this dual-cassette donor system could theoretically be expanded to other applications after further modification (Figure 4C), such as to simulate precise genome modifications, achieve conditional gene rescue or differentiate and analyze maternal, zygotic and paternal gene expression and activity.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about potential future applications of the dual-cassette donor system.

claim: The Ne-cassette can be engineered to contain a coding sequence with a precise mutation (such as a disease-causing point mutation) so that the deletion of the Po-cassette could conditionally simulate the precise mutation.
source: For example, the Ne-cassette can be engineered to contain a coding sequence with a precise mutation (such as a disease-causing point mutation) so that the deletion of the Po-cassette could conditionally simulate the precise mutation.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about a potential application of the dual-cassette donor system.

claim: Conditional gene rescue can be achieved by swapping the Po-cassette and Ne-cassette.
source: On the other hand, conditional gene rescue can be achieved by swapping the Po-cassette and Ne-cassette.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about a potential application of the dual-cassette donor system.

claim: The dual-cassette donor strategy may be utilized to study cell-autonomous and cell-non-autonomous gene functions.
source: This strategy may also be utilized to study cell-autonomous and cell-non-autonomous gene functions.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about a potential application of the strategy.

claim: The dual-cassette donor knockin strategy could theoretically be customized for use in other model systems, such as mice and Drosophila, or adapted for medical research.
source: Furthermore, our dual-cassette donor knockin strategy could theoretically be customized for use in other model systems, such as mice and Drosophila, or adapted for medical research, including the establishment of disease models for drug screening and mechanism dissection or the tracing of cancer cell transformation and metastasis to provide new insights into carcinogenesis and cancer therapy.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about the potential applicability of the strategy to other systems.

claim: The current dual-functional donor KI strategy has certain limitations and is open to further improvement.
source: Nevertheless, our current dual-functional donor KI strategy has certain limitations and is open to further improvement.
evidence: This is an acknowledgment of limitations in the current approach.

claim: Most intron sequences downstream of the Cas9/gRNA target sites as well as the endogenous 3'-UTRs have been omitted in the current donor design, and the strategy mainly relies on the downstream coding sequence from the cDNA to rescue the correct expression of the target gene.
source: To simplify donor design and construction and reduce the size of the donor plasmids as much as possible, we have omitted most intron sequences downstream of the Cas9/gRNA target sites as well as the endogenous 3'-UTRs, and mainly relied on the downstream coding sequence from the cDNA to rescue the correct expression of the target gene.
evidence: This is a description of a design choice and potential limitation of the current approach.

claim: The omission of introns and 3'-UTRs may alter the expression pattern and/or regulation of the target gene.
source: This approach may alter the expression pattern and/or regulation of the target gene, so we suggest careful evaluation of the reporter gene expression and comparison of the result with the endogenous gene characteristics before performing further experiments, such as conditional knockout or lineage tracing.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about a potential limitation of the donor design.

claim: The authors suggest careful evaluation of the reporter gene expression and comparison of the result with the endogenous gene characteristics before performing further experiments.
source: This approach may alter the expression pattern and/or regulation of the target gene, so we suggest careful evaluation of the reporter gene expression and comparison of the result with the endogenous gene characteristics before performing further experiments, such as conditional knockout or lineage tracing.
evidence: This is a recommendation based on awareness of potential limitations.

claim: Introns and 3'-UTRs can easily be included in the donor design when necessary.
source: Of course, one can easily include introns and 3'-UTRs in the donor design when necessary.
evidence: This is a statement about the flexibility of the donor design approach.

claim: The current approach may not be applicable to genes with multiple alternative splicing isoforms or genes regulated by RNA splicing.
source: On the other hand, since only one form of the downstream intronless cDNA sequence is inserted into the final KI allele to complement the disruption of endogenous genes, this approach may not be applicable to genes with multiple alternative splicing isoforms or genes regulated by RNA splicing.
evidence: This is a statement about a limitation of the current approach.

claim: The limitation regarding alternative splicing may be avoided by including all the downstream introns in the Po-cassette of the donor.
source: However, this limitation may be avoided by including all the downstream introns in the Po-cassette of the donor.
evidence: This is a suggestion for how to overcome a limitation of the current approach.

claim: The limitation regarding alternative splicing might sometimes be considered a unique advantage, through which KI alleles with different alternative splicing isoforms could be purposely designed and generated separately.
source: In addition, this limitation sometimes might be considered a unique advantage, through which KI alleles with different alternative splicing isoforms could be purposely designed and generated separately, facilitating specific and detailed investigation as well as the comparison of different isoforms.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about how a limitation could be turned into an advantage.

claim: All the current KI alleles retain the plasmid backbone sequence at the insertion site in the genome, which might induce DNA methylation and silencing of transcription.
source: In addition to the disadvantages in the design of the rescue sequences in the Po-cassette, another concern is that all the current KI alleles retain the plasmid backbone sequence at the insertion site in the genome, which might induce DNA methylation and silencing of transcription, as previously reported (Suzuki et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a statement about a potential problem with the current approach, supported by a citation.
